text:
marie: Quick Q — noticed a staging worker log that prints the first ~8 chars of a partner API key, e.g. `key=sk_live_abcd1234...`. It's landing in the staging S3 logs. Is that allowed? cc @sec-bot @oncall

atul: We avoid logging secret fragments beyond 4 chars. Who owns that worker? @jessie?

jessie: That’s my team. We added the fragment to help trace rate-limited requests across retries. We can change it, just looking for the recommended masking pattern that still lets us correlate events.

sec-bot: Policy reminder: do NOT log secrets >4 chars. Acceptable patterns: mask after prefix `sk_****` or show only last 2 chars `sk_***34`. Preferred: store a derived digest (HMAC/SHA) for correlation, not any raw substring. Also ensure the S3 bucket has server-side encryption + restricted ACLs. Filing note: create a security ticket if secrets were ever pushed to artifacts.

sam: For correlation you can do an HMAC: `digest = HMAC_SHA256(key, request_id)` and log `digest[:8]` instead of key parts. That gives a stable ID without exposing key material.

jessie: Copy. One more thing — the same key was accidentally included once in a debug bundle inside a build artifact (staging build). Do we need to rotate now or just remove the logs?

marie: If that was a partner key we have to treat it as compromised: rotate and notify partner + CS/legal. If it’s an internal service key, rotate and follow the internal rotation playbook. Either way remove logs ASAP.

oncall: I can rotate internal service creds. For partner-owned keys we need CS + legal sign-off before outreach. Immediate mitigation: delete offending objects from the bucket (object versioning?) and push mask patch. Rotation window: aim for 24h for internal, coordinate for partner keys.

atul: Also quick question about KMS/HSM — we wrap production keys in HSM. If we need to rebind a wrapped key for debugging in staging, what's the process and who can unbind? @sec-bot?

sec-bot: HSM unbind/unwrap operations require approval by the sec-approver group and an INFRA ticket. Staging generally uses envelope encryption with KMS grants; only infra-admins can request a temporary unwrap grant for debugging. Never hand raw keys to devs. All unwrap actions are audited and require justification.

jessie: Understood. Plan: 1) remove the sensitive substring from logs and replace with `digest[:8]` HMAC; 2) scrub S3 (delete objects + confirm no snapshots), 3) open INFRA ticket if we need a time-limited grant to correlate past events, 4) if partner key, coordinate rotation/notification with CS. I'll push a patch in a few mins.

marie: :thumbsup: Please drop PR link + ticket id here when ready.

jessie: PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/worker/pull/482 — masking + HMAC added. Ticket: INFRA-1234.

sam: :eyes: I’ll review the PR this afternoon.

oncall: Let me know once logs are scrubbed and rotation status. I’ll handle the internal rotation if needed.

marie: Thanks all — good catch.
